name: Greenland (Denmark)
summary: Greenland still applies the old Danish Inheritance Act of 1964, not the 2008 Danish act. I could not read its text, so the size of the protected share is not confirmed. Denmark is not in the Hague Trusts Convention, and I found no trust or private foundation law for Greenland.
reserved_share: Children and spouse have compulsory shares (tvangsarv) under the Danish tradition and the 1964 Greenland act; amounts and the article were not verified.
foreign_law_note: Not sourced. The Greenland act's conflict rules and Danish rules on foreign law were not read.
trust_note: Denmark is not listed in the HCCH table, and the Convention has not been extended to Greenland. No trust statute was found. Foundations (fonde) exist in Danish-based law; whether Greenland has its own foundation law that allows a family foundation was not checked.
open_questions: Inheritance Act for Greenland (Act 154 of 27 May 1964): the compulsory shares and article numbers were not read; forced_heirship 'yes' rests on the general Danish model and should be verified.

A 2017 parliamentary question said Greenland still used the old act and that the 2008 Danish act could be extended by royal decree; a 2022 Naalakkersuisut proposal on modernising inheritance law exists. The outcome is unknown; check for a new Greenland inheritance act.
Foundation (fond) and trust rules for Greenland were not sourced.
Trust/foundation availability marked unclear: no statute was found, which does not show that none exists.
